'''Osasere Benjamin''' "'''Oso'''" '''Ighodaro''' (born July 14, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]].

==Early life and high school career==
Born in [[Mesa, Arizona]], Ighodaro grew up in [[Chandler, Arizona|Chandler]] and attended [[Desert Vista High School]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Steele |first=Ben |date=September 19, 2019 |title=Get to know: 2020 Marquette commit Osasere 'Oso' Ighodaro |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2019/09/19/get-know-2020-marquette-commit-oso-ighodaro/2369265001/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=December 1, 2023 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}}</ref> He averaged 10 points, six rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game as a junior.<ref>{{cite web |last=Steele |first=Ben |date=August 10, 2019 |title=Marquette recruiting Q&A: 2020 forward Osa Ighodaro |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/2019/08/10/marquette-recruiting-q-a-2020-forward-osa-ighodaro/1974591001/ |access-date=December 1, 2023 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}}</ref> Ighodaro was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] over offers from [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]] and [[Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball|Vanderbilt]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |date=September 13, 2019 |title=Marquette basketball gets commitment from forward Osasere Ighodaro |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/recruiting/2019/09/13/marquette-basketball-recruiting-commitment-forward-osasere-ighodaro/2312860001/ |access-date=December 1, 2023 |work=[[The Arizona Republic]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Ighodaro played in five games during his true freshman season with the Marquette Golden Eagles before suffering an injury and using a medical [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Steele|title=Oso Ighodaro barely played as a freshman for Marquette. Two years later, Shaka Smart ready to empower him with big role.|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2022/11/07/marquette-basketball-coach-shaka-smart-will-use-oso-ighodaro-as-passer/69616098007/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=November 7, 2022|access-date=December 1, 2023}}</ref> He played in all 32 of Marquette's games and averaged 5.5 points per game during his redshirt freshman season. Ighodaro spent the following summer practicing to improve his passing and ball handling skills at the recommendation of coach [[Shaka Smart]] so that he could be a better fit in the Golden Eagles' starting lineup.<ref>{{cite web |last=Hamilton |first=Brian |date=January 12, 2023 |title='Unique' Oso Ighodaro is Marquette's most valuable asset in win over UConn |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4083815/2023/01/12/marquette-win-uconn-oso-ighodaro/ |access-date=December 1, 2023 |work=[[The Athletic]] |via=The New York Times}}</ref> As a redshirt sophomore he was named second team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East Conference]] after averaging 11.4 points, a team-high 5.9 rebounds, 3.3 assists and 1.5 blocks per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jamie|last=Shaw|title=Ten potential college basketball breakout stars|url=https://www.on3.com/news/ten-potential-college-basketball-breakout-stars/|website=On3.com|date=August 18, 2023|access-date=December 1, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Steele |first=Ben |date=March 5, 2023 |title=Marquette's Tyler Kolek makes all-Big East team while Golden Eagles' Oso Ighodaro and Kam Jones on second team |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2023/03/05/marquettes-tyler-kolek-oso-ighodaro-kam-jones-earn-big-east-honors/69973679007/ |access-date=December 1, 2023 |work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 27, 2024, Ighodaro was selected with the 40th overall pick by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]; however, immediately on draft night, he was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stanley |first1=Logan |last2=Coppola |first2=Chris |date=June 27, 2024 |title=Phoenix Suns acquire former Desert Vista product Osasere Ighodaro on Day 2 of NBA Draft |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2024/06/27/phoenix-suns-osasere-ighodaro-marquette-nba-draft/74237944007/ |access-date=June 28, 2024 |work=The Arizona Central}}</ref> On July 4, he signed with the Suns.<ref>{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=July 4, 2024 |title=Suns Sign Oso Ighodaro To Four-Year Contract |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/07/suns-sign-oso-ighodaro-to-four-year-contract.html |access-date=July 5, 2024 |work=HoopsRumors.com}}</ref> Ighodaro would make his NBA debut on October 24, recording two points, six rebounds and a block in over twelve minutes of play in the Suns' 116–113 overtime win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] held in the Clippers' new home arena, [[Intuit Dome]]. On January 28, 2025, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] to the [[Valley Suns]] of the [[NBA G League]],<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Phoenix Suns Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/nba/teams/Phoenix-Suns/23/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=January 29, 2025}}</ref> being recalled the next day, following a double-double performance of 18 points and 18 rebounds in a win over the [[Salt Lake City Stars]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Phoenix Suns|title=OFFICIAL: We have recalled Oso Ighodaro from the @GLeagueSuns. He posted 18 points and 18 rebounds last night at Salt Lake City.|number=1884748506813837319|user=Suns|date=January 29, 2025|access-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref>

Ighodaro played in all 82 games (including 24 starts) for Phoenix during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 6.5 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 2.3 assists.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Ighodaro is of [[Nigerian]] descent.<ref>{{cite news|first=C. J.|last=Moore|title=How Oso Ighodaro developed into the linchpin of Marquette's beautiful offense|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5134630/2023/12/19/oso-ighodaro-marquette-basketball/|work=The New York Times|issn=0362-4331|date=December 19, 2023|access-date=October 28, 2024}}</ref> Despite growing up in the state of Arizona, he was not a fan of the [[Phoenix Suns]] at the time due to their poor play throughout the 2010s.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dana|last=Scott|title=How Devin Booker, Kevin Durant are connecting with young Phoenix Suns players|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2024/10/04/booker-durant-suns-youngest-valley-natives-inspire-each-other/75499825007/|website=AZCentral.com|date=October 4, 2024|access-date=January 31, 2025}}</ref>
